# GitHub Work Item Discovery

Scans participant `git-repository` entities that point at GitHub, calls the GitHub API (via the `gh` CLI) to list open issues in each repository, and upserts each issue as a `git-work-item` entity keyed by the stable name path `["github", owner, repo, "work-items", number]`. Pull requests are skipped. Issue timelines are optionally walked to link commits and other artifacts.

## Configuration

Read from the tool entity's top-level properties:

| Key | Type | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `max-items` | integer | Maximum issues to fetch per repository. Defaults to `200`. |

Authentication is delegated to the ambient `gh` CLI (or the injected `issueListRunner`/`timelineRunner` in tests); no token is stored on the tool entity.

## Usage

Wire the tool via a `tool-relationship`:

- `participants.tool` — the entity-id of this tool entity.
- `participants.target` — one or more `git-repository` entities whose owner/repo point at github.com.
- `participants.schedule` — a `schedule` entity governing how often issues are refreshed.

Set `paused: true` on the relationship to disable it. Non-GitHub `git-repository` participants are silently skipped, so the same relationship can safely span a mixed portfolio.
